Subject: AWS Marketplace settlement routing & entitlement questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — DataForge is excited to move forward with Redwood as our inference partner. Legal and finance have a couple of operational questions about how the AWS Marketplace listing will map to our internal billing: 

1) Entitlement mapping: We need clarity on how buyer entitlements (AWS SaaS entitlement) map to Redwood SKUs. Specifically, we track two internal SKUs: "DF-Inference-Standard" (metered per inference second) and "DF-Inference-FeaturePack" (monthly seat). Can AWS buyer entitlements be routed so settlement shows these two line items?

2) Settlement & invoice routing: Our procurement requires invoices to flow to procurement@dataforge.com and for AWS payout/settlement statements to reconcile to our internal PO numbers. Do you support configured invoice routing or a fulfillment hook to include our PO?

3) Usage reporting cadence & reconciliation: We need daily usage snapshots and a path for out-of-band adjustments if we notice discrepancies.

Attached: DF_AWS_SaaS_Contract_SOW_v3.pdf with proposed PO cadence.

Can you outline the technical steps and the expected timelines so I can close this on our side?

Thanks,
Rebecca Lin
Head of Procurement
DataForge Inc

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace settlement routing & entitlement questions

Hi Rebecca — great questions, and glad DataForge liked the demo. High level answers below; see details and next actions after.

1) Entitlement mapping: Yes — AWS Marketplace SaaS metering + entitlement flow can be mapped to two Redwood invoice line items. We implement a mapping layer during fulfillment where the AWS buyer entitlement (Marketplace entitlement ID) is translated into Redwood SKU IDs. For your case we will map:
  - Marketplace dimension "inference_seconds" -> Redwood SKU "DF-Inference-Standard" (metered hourly aggregation by default)
  - Marketplace dimension "feature_pack_monthly" -> Redwood SKU "DF-Inference-FeaturePack" (monthly entitlement, 1 per linked buyer account)

2) Invoice routing & PO injection: Redwood supports a fulfillment hook so that when we create the customer contract record (via the SaaS Contracts API / Fulfillment API) we pass buyer metadata including PO and invoice routing email. That metadata appears in our billing export and can be included in the invoice PDF we attach to the settlement bundle. For AWS settlement itself, the Marketplace payout includes a billing reference to your buyer account; we will include your PO in the line-item memo so your accounting team can easily reconcile.

3) Usage cadence & adjustments: We can provide daily usage files via a secure S3 bucket (CSV) and also push webhook deltas to a reconciliation endpoint you provide. For adjustments we support a manual adjustment workflow: you raise a reconciliation ticket -> we validate within 3 business days -> if confirmed we emit an out-of-band credit which appears on the next monthly invoice.

Next steps / timeline (proposed):
- Today/Tomorrow: Redwood and DataForge exchange AWS Marketplace Buyer IDs and the test buyer account (you can provide sandbox account)
- +3 business days: Redwood config team creates entitlement mapping and a test fulfillment entry (sandbox)
- +5 business days: Validate sample settlement payloads (we'll send a CSV with mapped SKU line items)
- +7-10 business days: Move to production listing and verify first settlement run

I've attached our pricing schedule XLSX so you can confirm line item codes on your side. Marcus, Karthik — can you own the sandbox fulfillment config and confirm the expected payload format? Vanessa, can you confirm whether we need a special invoice template for DataForge?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Partner Success — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: AWS Marketplace settlement routing & entitlement questions

Thanks Naomi — I'll take the sandbox config. Quick technical notes for the team and for DataForge to be aware of: 

- AWS Fulfillment: We'll use the AWS SaaS Fulfillment API to create entitlement records. The payload includes: productCode, dimension, customerIdentifier (AWS buyer id), and marketplace-entitlement-id. We map dimension -> Redwood SKU in our fulfillment service.
- Metering dimension choices: For meter-based SKU we recommend using a "cumulative seconds" dimension and run hourly aggregation on our side. This reduces the number of meter calls AWS requires and aligns with your billing model.
- Invoice routing: We'll add a custom field "buyerPO" to the contract metadata and include it in the invoice export (PDF and CSV). For Marketplace settlement, AWS's payout will still reference their internal buyer ID but our export will include the buyerPO so your finance team can match records.
- Reconciliation: We'll publish daily CSV to an S3 path s3://redwood-reports/dataforge/DF-114/usage/YYYY-MM-DD.csv (we'll send IAM role grant for read-only access). We'll also offer a signed webhook if you prefer push.

Action items:
- DataForge: share test buyer ID and sample PO format
- Marcus: provision sandbox fulfillment and send sample CSV by EOD Thursday
- Karthik: validate invoice template for inclusion of buyerPO

I'll kick off the sandbox now and will send sample payloads once ready.

— Marcus
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
